questions.q: What does Oracle recommend using instead of plain VARCHAR?
options: VARCHAR2, since Oracle reserves plain VARCHAR for potential future behavior changes
CLOB, for all string data regardless of size
TEXT, matching MySQL's naming
NVARCHAR, matching SQL Server's naming
questions.explain: Oracle's own documentation reserves VARCHAR for future changes and recommends VARCHAR2 as the real, supported variable-length type.

questions.q: What is Oracle's CLOB type for?
options: Storing binary image data only
A synonym for VARCHAR2 with no practical difference
Large text data, filling a role similar to SQL Server's VARCHAR(MAX) or older TEXT/NTEXT
A numeric type for very large integers
questions.explain: CLOB (Character Large Object) is Oracle's type for large text content.

questions.q: Which MySQL types form a sized family alongside TEXT for different maximum lengths?
options: MINITEXT, MAXTEXT, and ULTRATEXT
SHORTTEXT, STANDARDTEXT, and EXTENDEDTEXT
SMALLTEXT, BIGTEXT, and HUGETEXT
TINYTEXT, MEDIUMTEXT, and LONGTEXT
questions.explain: MySQL offers TINYTEXT, TEXT, MEDIUMTEXT, and LONGTEXT as a sized family of large-text types.

questions.q: What is distinctive about PostgreSQL's TEXT type compared to VARCHAR?
options: TEXT has no practical length limit, and there's little to no performance difference between VARCHAR and TEXT in PostgreSQL
TEXT can only store numeric data in PostgreSQL, not character data
TEXT is always slower than VARCHAR in PostgreSQL, so VARCHAR should always be preferred
PostgreSQL does not have a TEXT type at all
questions.explain: PostgreSQL's TEXT is unlimited in length with essentially no performance cost compared to VARCHAR, unlike some other platforms.

questions.q: In SQL Server, what is the core distinction between VARCHAR and NVARCHAR?
options: VARCHAR is for numbers and NVARCHAR is for text
NVARCHAR is deprecated in favor of VARCHAR in all modern SQL Server versions
VARCHAR stores non-Unicode character data; NVARCHAR stores Unicode data at 2 bytes per character
There is no difference; they are interchangeable aliases
questions.explain: The Unicode vs. non-Unicode distinction is the lens this lesson uses to compare every other platform's string types.
